chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His words: 'The fasting one is with the choice until the decline of the sun', he said: 'That is regarding the Obligatory [fasting]. But as for the Optional [fasting], then for him is that he breaks [his fast] at any hour he desires until the setting of the sun.'
ai.seo_question: When can a person break their optional fast compared to their obligatory fast?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key juristic distinction between the strict temporal limits of obligatory fasting and the flexibility of voluntary fasting. While the obligatory fast binds the believer until midday (Zawal), allowing for the nullification of the day's intent, the Nafl fast permits breaking at any hour before sunset, reflecting the leniency granted for voluntary acts of worship. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intention (Niyyah) as the cornerstone of fasting validity.
